ai.description: The Anamallai Night Frog (Nyctibatrachus deccanensis) is a small, brown-colored frog. It features a pointed snout and prominent, fleshy femoral glands. It is endemic to the Western Ghats.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Nyctibatrachus deccanensis* is best distinguished by its distinctively pointed, elongated snout and the presence of prominent, fleshy digital discs on its fingers and toes.
ai.habitat: The Anamallai Night Frog inhabits high-altitude evergreen rainforests and shola grasslands in the Western Ghats, typically found near streams at elevations above 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Anamallai night frog is strictly nocturnal, remaining hidden in rock crevices or under leaf litter during the day to avoid predators and desiccation.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Nyctibatrachus deccanensis* breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of large, unpigmented eggs on wet rocks near streams, which undergo direct development.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Anamallai Night Frog is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, specifically found in the Anamalai Hills of Tamil Nadu and Kerala at elevations of 800–1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Anamallai Night Frog produces a series of high-pitched, rhythmic "ticking" or "chirping" sounds, typically heard near fast-flowing streams in rainforest habitats.
